questions.q: What is the main purpose of fingerprinting the training data in a model card?
options: To encrypt the training data
To make the model train faster
To trace a model to the exact data it was trained on, so two people can confirm they used the same data
To reduce the model's AUC variance
questions.explain: A content hash acts as a label for the data: if any value changes, the fingerprint changes. It supports lineage but is not a security control.

questions.q: In the subgroup check, premium customers have an AUC of 0.664 on 201 rows with about 11 cancellations. How should this be reported?
options: As proof the model is unfair to premium customers
With the group size and a caveat that the estimate is very uncertain
It should be omitted from documentation
As proof the model is perfect for premium customers
questions.explain: With only about 11 positive cases, AUC for that group can swing widely. Reporting n alongside the score prevents over-reading.

questions.q: Basic-plan customers are flagged at 33.4% versus 6.0% for premium. Their real cancel rates are 16.2% and 5.5%. What does this suggest?
options: The flagging follows genuine differences in cancellation risk, which is expected, though it still belongs in the review
The model is randomly flagging customers
The training data was corrupted
Premium customers should be flagged more
questions.explain: The model flags more of the group that really cancels more. Documenting this lets reviewers decide whether that is acceptable for the intended use.

questions.q: Which field of a model card tells reviewers what the model must NOT be used for?
options: metrics
software
training_data
out_of_scope
questions.explain: Intended use and out-of-scope use together define the approved purpose of the model and guard against misuse.

questions.q: Why is the audit log written as an append-only file with one JSON record per decision?
options: So decisions are recorded in order and are not edited after the fact
So it can be read faster by pandas
Because JSON cannot store approvals otherwise
So the model can retrain itself
questions.explain: An append-only trail preserves who approved what and when. In real teams the same information often lives in pull-request reviews or protected environments.
